source_text:
(73) Στίχ. ιθ΄. Καὶ ἔῤῥηξεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸ τραῦμα τὸ ἐν σιαγόνι, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὕδωρ.
Ἀντὶ τοῦ· Ἔῤῥηξε τῇ πληγῇ τῆς σιαγόνος τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὕδατα.
orientation: Origen opens his Notes on Judges by quoting Judges 15:19 and then giving an alternative reading of the same verse.
pass_a_gloss: [Verse] 19. And God broke the wound, the [one] in [the] jawbone, and water came out from it. Instead of: He split by the blow of the jawbone the earth, and waters came out.

choices.why: The verb means to break or burst; 'broke' keeps the literal force for God's action on the wound.
In the alternative reading πληγή is the instrument of the splitting, so 'blow' fits the sense of a striking action.
This phrase introduces the alternative reading; 'Instead of' marks the contrast clearly.

bible_refs.note: Καὶ ἔῤῥηξεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸ τραῦμα τὸ ἐν σιαγόνι, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὕδωρ

pass_b_english: Judges 15:19: “And God broke the wound in the jawbone, and water came out of it.” Instead of this, it means: He split the earth by the blow of the jawbone, and waters came out.
